tests.name: Accessibility service registered in AndroidManifest
tests.evidence: AndroidManifest.xml declares ClipboardAccessibilityService with BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission, intent filter, and meta-data pointing to accessibility_service_config.xml

tests.name: Service appears in system Accessibility Settings
tests.evidence: Navigated to Settings > Accessibility > Downloaded apps. 'Cache Vault Dev' listed as an accessibility service.

tests.name: Service description shows in system settings
tests.evidence: Service detail page shows: 'Saves clipboard content to this phone's vault automatically. No notification to tap — copies are captured silently and stored locally.'

tests.name: Standard Android confirmation dialog appears
tests.evidence: Tapping 'Use Cache Vault Dev' triggers system dialog: 'Allow Cache Vault Dev to have full control of your device?' with Allow/Deny buttons.

tests.name: Service starts and registers clipboard listener
tests.evidence: After tapping Allow, logcat shows: 'ClipA11y: clipboard listener registered via accessibility service'. System settings confirms service enabled: enabled_accessibility_services contains our service.

tests.name: App Settings UI shows 'Automatic capture is on'
tests.evidence: Settings > Capture on this phone section shows: 'Automatic capture is on — copies are saved silently.' instead of the 'Enable automatic capture' button.

tests.name: ClipboardWatch skips notification when accessibility is active
tests.evidence: Code review: ClipboardWatch.onChanged() checks ClipboardAccessibilityService.isEnabled() and returns early before posting the notification.

tests.name: ClipboardCapture.capture() function works end-to-end
tests.evidence: The same ClipboardCapture.capture() function the accessibility service calls was verified to work via share intent test (saved 'TestClipStandaloneVaultWorks123' to vault with sensitivity detection). The accessibility service calls this exact function with vaultLocked=false.

tests.name: End-to-end automatic clipboard capture from another app
tests.reason: ADB cannot set the clipboard on this emulator. Tried: clipper broadcast (app not installed), cmd clipboard (not available), service call clipboard (too complex), Ctrl+A/Ctrl+C with meta state (not interpreted as Ctrl), long-press on Chrome text (no context menu), double/triple-tap on EditText (adds characters instead of selecting), KEYCODE_COPY (no effect). The clipboard change listener IS registered and active (confirmed by logcat), but ADB cannot trigger the clipboard change event it listens for. This is an ADB/emulator limitation, not an app issue.

conclusion: The accessibility service is fully implemented, registered, enabled, and running. The clipboard listener is active (logcat confirms). The capture function it calls (ClipboardCapture.capture) is proven to work via the share intent path. The only unverified step is the end-to-end clipboard change triggering the service's capture — blocked by ADB's inability to set the clipboard on the emulator. A physical device test would close this gap.
